pr_title: Fix circle scale not matching stable due to missing multiplier
pr_comments:
Test failures here are gonna suck...

The diffcalc changes I guess are expected and can be locally undone, but this also appears to be impacting hyperdashing. So this is gonna need a crossreference against stable. I'll see what I can get done there...

The above is from superficial review. Remaining questions in my head:

- cross-check hitcircle behaviour against stable
- cross-check catcher behaviour (and hyperdash generation) against stable
- make a diffcalc sheet and decide if we care enough to undo the changes locally to diffcalc or just roll forward with hopefully minimally changed values

Okay so I did just a bit of further work on this and here is what follows from empirical evidence:

### osu! input radius

[OsuRadiusTest.zip](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/13029270/OsuRadiusTest.zip) contains a beatmap (`OsuRadiusTest.osu`) and two replays (`OsuHit`, `OsuMiss`). The replays were created as follows:

```csharp
private const float FudgeInside = 1.0004f;
private const float FudgeMiddle = 1.00041f;
private const float FudgeOutside = 1.00042f;

// `OsuHit`

new OsuReplayFrame(0, new Vector2(-256, 500)),
new OsuReplayFrame(3000, new Vector2(OsuHitObject.OBJECT_RADIUS * 0.5f * FudgeInside, 0), OsuAction.LeftButton),
new OsuReplayFrame(3001, new Vector2(OsuHitObject.OBJECT_RADIUS * 0.5f * FudgeInside, 0))

// `OsuMissed`

new OsuReplayFrame(0, new Vector2(-256, 500)),
new OsuReplayFrame(3000, new Vector2(OsuHitObject.OBJECT_RADIUS * 0.5f * FudgeOutside, 0), OsuAction.LeftButton),
new OsuReplayFrame(3001, new Vector2(OsuHitObject.OBJECT_RADIUS * 0.5f * FudgeOutside, 0))
```

**Results:**

| Replay | stable | master | this PR (with patches above applied) |
| :- | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| `OsuHit` | ✔️ hit | ❌ miss | ✔️ hit |
| `OsuMiss` | ❌ miss | ❌ miss | ❌ miss |

**Conclusion:** This PR is conclusively more correct.

### catch hyperdash generation

[CatchHyperTests.zip](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/13029273/CatchHyperTests.zip) contains two beatmaps: `CatchNoHyper.osu` and `CatchHyper.osu`. They both have two hitobjects, and only differ in that `CatchHyper`'s second hitobject is shifted 1 unit to the right.

**Results:**

| Beatmap | stable | master | this PR (with patches above applied) |
| :- | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| `CatchHyper` | ⏩ first fruit is hyper | ⏩ first fruit is hyper | ⏩ first fruit is hyper |
| `CatchNoHyper` | ❌ no hyperfruit | ❌ no hyperfruit | ❌ no hyperfruit |

**Conclusion:** No perceivable difference in constructed test case.

In testing, shifting the coordinates of the second object by sub-unit amounts did nothing. This is likely due to the flooring that stable applies. That also means that the results of this test may be overly optimistic and mismatches may occur on certain sub-unit alignments. I probably wouldn't go too deep into it in this PR.

### catcher capturing width

[CatchRangeTests.zip](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/13029275/CatchRangeTests.zip) contains two replays for `CatchNoHyper` above: `Catch.osr` and `NoCatch.osr`, generated as such:

```csharp
// NoCatch
new CatchReplayFrame(0, 0),
new CatchReplayFrame(3000, catcherWidthFudge * 0.8f - 0.001f)

// Catch
new CatchReplayFrame(0, 0),
new CatchReplayFrame(3000, catcherWidthFudge * 0.8f)
```

These were chosen to satisfy stable - the `Catch` replay should catch the first fruit, and the `NoCatch` one should miss everything.

**Results:**

| Replay | stable | master | this PR (with patches above applied) |
| :- | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| `Catch` | ✔️ first fruit caught | ✔️ first fruit caught | ✔️ first fruit caught |
| `NoCatch` | ❌ nothing caught | ✔️ first fruit caught | ✔️ first fruit caught |

**Conclusion:** lazer is wrong, but is probably made no more wrong by this PR and this should be handled separately if anything.

---

In short, next step is probably a sheet and seeing the impact on SR this has. If it's not too egregious, we can probably proceed with this as-is.
Thanks for the extended checking. I've applied the two proposed changes.

> Oh also diffcalc tests need to be fixed.

That's what the diffcalc runs are for - to ensure that we can just do that and not inadvertently cause some weird star rating/pp jumps ;)
Quite a few large changes in the catch spreadsheet. Worth looking into to see if they can be justified.

I dunno. Sounds like the old values were just wrong? Probably means hyperdashes were being generated where they shouldn't.

I'd probably do a comparison of the beatmap and look for any differences like that.

Should I be doing this or are you already looking into it @smoogipoo ?
I'm not looking into this at the moment. By-beatmap-comparison is the way I'd go about it as well.

While I didn't find any immediate changes in the beatmaps (I may have overlooked something), @bdach brought it to my attention that this isn't actually applied to catch in stable code. I've removed the usage of the fudge factor there as a result, and updated the osu! diffcalc tests to fix the fractional differences.

issue_context.title: Edge hit note becomes a miss when watching back replay
issue_context.body:
### Type

Game behaviour

### Bug description

I was watching back Akolibed's play on Reign of Fear (https://osu.ppy.sh/scores/osu/4518727921) when I discovered that he misses at 1270 combo in lazer, but not in stable. I dug a little deeper using 2 replay parsing apps, and osu! rewind displays the lazer behaviour (a miss), and circleguard displays the stable behaviour (a hit).



### Screenshots or videos

osu! rewind:
![image](https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/92956514/bef1c703-76b3-48fe-9ca8-ffd219d1f265)

circleguard:
![image](https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/92956514/e45f3e96-96ab-4b77-808e-49be4df7c584)

Lazer:
https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/92956514/8e83a596-f646-458f-8a94-dea115ff9eb8

Stable:
https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/92956514/b28ac5aa-868a-4536-873a-fb22ffc6f80e



### Version

2023.1008.1-lazer

comments:
My immediate guess, without looking at the replay or anything in detail, would be floating point differences in the hitradius calculation.

[circleguard](https://github.com/circleguard/circlecore/blob/659f099c5653a15a90a749379cd0bca63376ab61/circleguard/utils.py#L220)

```python
def hitradius(CS):
    # attempting to match stable hitradius
    return np.float32(64 * ((1.0 - np.float32(0.7) * (float(np.float32(CS)) - 5) / 5)) / 2) * np.float32(1.00041)
```


[rewind](https://github.com/abstrakt8/rewind/blob/a815a67f75c28a995b5251f34071c044abaa8faa/libs/osu/math/src/difficulty.ts#L7)

```javascript
export function circleSizeToScale(CS: number) {
  return float32((1.0 - (0.7 * (CS - 5)) / 5) / 2);
}
```

[lazer](https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/e927267c4d66e29ea0eaa894eda1b5da4adb98b1/osu.Game.Rulesets.Osu/Objects/OsuHitObject.cs#L158)

```csharp
            Scale = (1.0f - 0.7f * (difficulty.CircleSize - 5) / 5) / 2
```

[stable](https://github.com/peppy/osu-stable-reference/blob/1531237b63392e82c003c712faa028406073aa8f/osu!/GameplayElements/Beatmaps/BeatmapDifficultyCalculatorOsu.cs#L52) (I think?)

```csharp
            float circleRadius = (PLAYFIELD_WIDTH / 16.0f) * (1.0f - 0.7f * (float)HitObjectManager.AdjustDifficulty(Beatmap.DifficultyCircleSize));
```

I'll be honest with you...I have no idea anymore where some of the casts or constants in the circleguard code came from (what is `np.float32(1.00041)` doing there??). But maybe this will be useful for anyone looking into this. Circleguard has matched stable in all cases I know of, fwiw.

Path forward would be to reimplement to match stable calculation-wise, I believe. Should try and simplify the equation down as much as possible.

Will add this to the project as it seems important.

review_comments: I had a feeling this was possible but brain was off at this point.
